name: Mount Wilson Observatory
place: Mount Wilson, San Gabriel Mountains, California
description: A historic observatory above Los Angeles, first funded by the Carnegie Institution in 1904, with the 100-inch Hooker telescope (completed 1917) and the CHARA interferometer array. It now combines research with public tours and observing nights.
highlights: In 1923 Edwin Hubble showed with the Hooker telescope that the Andromeda nebula lies outside the Milky Way.
In 1929 Edwin Hubble and Milton Humason demonstrated that the universe is expanding.
The 100-inch was the world's largest telescope until 1949.
